summary: Mobility is stabilising near pre‑pandemic levels with an MF‑Index of 74, but public transport usage remains 24% below 2019 levels. Fuel savings are strong, yet uneven work‑from‑home adoption creates sectoral risk and equity concerns. Targeted policy tweaks can lock in gains and steer a sustainable modal shift.

signals.detail: Weekly fuel savings of 35.7 million litres represent 42% of the MCO peak, reflecting the effectiveness of high fuel prices and the fuel policy component scoring 100. The savings help curb emissions but indicate that consumption is still far above the 2021 low point, leaving room for further efficiency measures.

Daily PT trips total 1.09 million, roughly 76% of the pre‑pandemic daily average (1.43 million). The ridership component of the MF‑Index is 76.1, signalling a modest rebound but still a notable shortfall that could push commuters toward private cars if not addressed.

Logistics, construction and retail sectors show mobility scores above 90 and WFH adoption below 15%, exposing them to higher fuel cost volatility and congestion risk. This uneven exposure could dampen productivity gains as fuel prices stay elevated.

WFH adoption varies sharply: 60% in public/GLC entities versus only 8% in logistics and 5% in construction. The disparity creates unequal commuting burdens and limits the overall emissions benefit of remote work policies.

High fuel prices (RON95 RM 4.57/L) and strong fuel savings encourage a shift away from private cars, yet PT ridership remains below pre‑pandemic levels, suggesting a partial but incomplete modal transition. Sustained incentives are needed to lock in a lasting shift.

recommendation: Introduce a tiered PT fare subsidy to lift daily ridership to at least 80% of the 2019 baseline by 2027, while expanding flexible‑work incentives in logistics, construction and retail to raise sectoral WFH rates to 25%. Maintain the current fuel tax structure to preserve weekly savings and set a target of a 10% further reduction in fuel consumption within the next year.
